correctness.rationale: The frozen proof fails at RESULT.md line 80: the extra common-edge count is not bounded in expectation by the extra count in one tree. At n=2 the finite pair is always an edge, and it is common in the infinite parent graphs with probability (1/2)^2; the excess 3/4 exceeds H_2−1=1/2. In the full replacement /workspace/repairs/1/RESULT.md the excess is instead bounded by the sum of the two sample excesses, so its expectation is at most 2(H_n^{harmonic}−1), still o(n). Re-audit of the unchanged kernel: for i<j with priorities u<v, the nearest lower priority on the left must be i (all d−1 interior priorities exceed v), and any first lower priority to the right must be below u so that i wins the parent comparison. Its priority, if present, is uniform below v, giving the factor u/v+(1−u/v)(1−v)^{n−j}. The beta integral and reflected orientation give the exact kernel; direct binary-insertion enumeration independently checked every oriented frequency for n=2 through 7. For the square expansion, a cross term uses sum_{d≤s}1/[d(d+1)]=s/(s+1), and the two boundary indices obey s+t≥n. Partial fractions give sum a_d²=2ζ(2)−3 and sum d a_d²=2−ζ(2); tails give the stated error, since one index in the double boundary sum is at least n/2. On the integers the nearest lower priority on each side exists almost surely; taking finite intervals growing to the integers makes the tested parent relation eventually constant and gives the interior edge probability a_d. The shared right-edge count per vertex is a bounded shift-equivariant function of two independent i.i.d. arrays, so the ergodic theorem gives L¹ convergence of its spatial mean. Retaining both endpoints of an infinite edge retains the winning parent in the nearest-lower rule; omission of outside candidates cannot displace it. The repaired two-sample bound controls internal extras, and at most d starting positions can give right-crossing edges of length d, whose expected count summed over d is bounded by sum d a_d². After division by n both errors vanish. This proves the same scientific result in the repaired file, without calling L¹ convergence a strong law.
residual_risks: The theorem is for independent random insertion orders, not uniform shapes or ancestor pairs; it asserts L¹ convergence and gives no CLT or variance estimate.

evidence: Holmgren–Janson sum single-tree fringe functionals and give limit laws for those sums. Bóna–Burghart–Wagner use independent uniform spanning trees of a graph and obtain a Poisson limit of mean two for K_n.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The first functional has no independent second BST with the same key labels. The latter framework samples uniformly from spanning trees; a BST generated by a random permutation is neither uniform over all labelled spanning trees nor given by that model's assumptions. Their conclusions do not cover the two-BST mean or its density.

originality.rationale: The repair leaves the statistical claim unchanged. The known ancestor calculation, local fringe-function limit theory, common leaf-interval edges in uniform Catalan trees, and common labelled edges in uniform or recursive tree ensembles do not supply this random-permutation direct-edge kernel and the resulting two-term mean and limiting density. The strongest adjacent indexed claim uses the same BST model but a maximum shared fringe interval, not direct adjacency. The pass is bounded to the distinct calculation and law, not the priority representation or ergodic method.
residual_risks: Unexamined treap and Cartesian-tree results might contain the kernel or an equivalent calculation; a bounded search does not prove priority. The comparison to the Catalan-tree fraction uses the inspected table, not its separately cited proof.

value.rationale: The canonical random-permutation tree law is label-inhomogeneous near boundaries. The exact two-sided direct-edge kernel makes finite overlap calculable, resolves how independence can still leave a positive macroscopic fraction of identical labelled adjacencies, and quantifies the finite-size correction. A researcher comparing random tree models or checking random-BST overlap simulations has a precise benchmark, distinguishable from shape, fringe and ancestor overlap. The repaired bound preserves both exact formulas and the density law.
residual_risks: This is a first-order concentration statement rather than a fluctuation theory, and is not claimed for correlated samples.
